name: Cholon
summary: The Chinese district of Saigon, and the French swimming pool where Larry and his friends went when they were off duty: "Because we were Radio Operators we couldn't get KP duty or anything so when we were off, we were to be relaxing. Ron Tototz, Zukowski and that guy who played the guitar would go here." The pool is in VN-0004, VN-0005, VN-0075 and VN-0083. Cholon was also a stop on the way out at the end of his tour: after the medic told him he had yellow jaundice, "the next day they place me in Cholon near where the French swimming pool was at for maybe 3 days and then they flew me to Subic Bay in the Philippines."
researchNotes: Recollections: giscus-vn-0004-c18035138, -vn-0005-c18035136 (paraphrase) and -c18035487, -vn-0075-c18259881, -vn-0083-c18259885 and -c18259904, giscus-stories-c18259364 (the medevac route). 2026-08-23 (giscus-stories-c18118999, paraphrase): the pool was "near Binh Choi, which is south of the airport near Cholon"; "Binh Choi" is phonetic and not yet matched to a period place name. The 'French swimming pool' most plausibly refers to one of the colonial pool facilities that survived into the American period; period Saigon guides and veteran accounts of Cholon recreation spots could identify it, and the English FIRST AID signage visible in VN-0004/VN-0005 is a check. 2026-09-05: an unplaced fragment, "I met some Thai soldiers that were different personalities. This may have been by the pool in Cholon" (giscus-vn-0041-c18308745); his son records it was a separate story told while looking at a mountain photograph. Thai military personnel in South Vietnam in 1964–65 were few, which makes the encounter datable in principle. 2026-09-14: this record's summary said he swam with Ron and a friend whose name he could not recall; the friend is the guitar player of VN-0003 (giscus-vn-0005-c18035487), whose name is still an open question. VN-0076's bilingual shop signs, which he placed at the Continental in Saigon, are noted on that photograph; the link from that comment to this place was removed 2026-09-14, since he placed it in Saigon. 2026-09-15, standard public place names (his son's rule, CLAUDE.md "Place names"): the Vietnamese spelling Chợ Lớn shows only as the vietnameseName line; removed from the alternate names.
